text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas reads like a Marner season with the volume turned up on one side: 25 assists, 4 goals. That's 29 points in 24 games, on a pace that tops our talent range for him.

The assists are earned. He's a setup man by every measure we have, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 83rd percentile for primary shot assists last season, with 62% of his zone exits leaving with the puck. Vegas controls 56% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him out there.

The goals are the odd part. He has 4 on 6.9 expected, shooting 6.5% against a talent range of roughly 11 to 15%, and that's the kind of gap that tends to close. He keeps getting the looks. If they start going in while the assists hold, his season projection of around 91 points stops looking generous.

For a player who left Toronto with so much said about him, the quiet version of this story is probably the best one: he's doing exactly what he was brought in to do.
headline: Marner is setting the table, not finishing
